newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lowest French wheat bid seen worth $157 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: Lowest French wheat bid seen worth $157 a tonne.

text.p: The lowest export bid through France for European Union soft wheat on Thursday valued spot Rouen wheat at around $157 per tonne, traders said.
Local wheat prices gained about five francs a tonne to 860 francs a tonne (excluding carrying charges) for December on news traders had bid for more than a million tonnes of EU wheat.
"It's a surprise, someone has done something," said one trader. "It's Russia," said another, adding there was market talk a top U.S. grain firm had sold wheat to Russian buyers.
The lowest subsidy bid of 16.47 Ecus valued French wheat at $157 a tonne once the price reaction was taken into account.
ONIC cereals office said traders bid through France for 1,322,200 tonnes of European Union free-market soft wheat at refunds between 16.47 and 21.74 Ecus per tonne.
Traders bid through Germany for 206,200 tonnes of wheat at rebates of 16.73 to 18.93 Ecus per tonne, traders there said.
Britain's grain authority reported some bidding but gave no details.
